method.producer: One separate public preparation process per size; excluded from receiving samples.
method.receiver: Three serial fresh Node main-isolate processes per size. Imports, observer and positive control precede baseline; encoded input and prior receiver state have separate GC baselines.
method.allocation: In-process inspector statistical allocation sampling covers only public restore plus observer/runtime work within its interval; stopped before independent semantic checks. Includes requested major/minor collected-object options; raw requested parameters and actual returned profile are recorded.
method.polling: Before/after public call and 5ms event-loop polls. Blocking work and intervals can hide higher transient use; maxima are observed full-process/isolate readings, never exact or component peaks.
method.privateObservation: Installed getExecutionOwner read only to create WeakRef witnesses. No owner, scheduler, generator, limits or production instrumentation is modified.
method.childEnvironment: Only PATH, TMPDIR, LANG, LC_ALL inherited. No full heap or unrelated process inputs collected.
method.childWallLimit: 180 seconds per owned producer/receiver process, then SIGTERM and after one second SIGKILL if still open. Timeout/signal/missing reports are retained as failures; the native operation deadline stays 60 seconds.

limitations: Sampling quantities are statistical profiler outputs, not exact allocations, exclusive retained components or simultaneous peak bytes.
Whole receiving-process readings include the held encoding string, prior/current state, garbage, observer, inspector and runtime. Fields overlap; do not sum external/ArrayBuffer/RSS.
WeakRef witnesses establish only observed collection of listed object roots under this explicit GC policy. Strings, every descendant, normal unforced GC and general leak freedom remain unqualified.
Source-reindex restore, mutation/encoder exact peak, browser/worker/transport buffers and conditional collector-accurate component retention remain outside this native receiving slice.
No native portability, new capacity limit, physical-device, AT, browser or publication claim is made.
